{{Start date and age|df=yes|2019}} (as ''Gaziantep Futbol Kulübü'') | stadium = [[Gaziantep Stadium]] | capacity = 30,320 | coordinates = {{Coord|37.123889|37.3825|format=dms|type:landmark_scale:3000_region:TR|display=it}} | president = Memik Yılmaz | manager = [[Orhan Ak]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | league = {{Turkish football updater|Gaziantep FK}} | season = {{Turkish football updater|Gaziantep FK2}} | position = {{Turkish football updater|Gaziantep FK3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.gaziantepfk.org/}} | current = 2026–27 Gaziantep F.K. season | pattern_b1 = _gfk2223h | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _gfk2223a | pattern_b2 = _gfk2324a | pattern_ra2 = _gfk2223a | shorts2 = ffffff | socks2 = ffffff | pattern_b3 = _gfk2324t | pattern_la3 = _gazi2324t | pattern_ra3 = _gfk2324t | shorts3 = 000000 | socks3 = 000000 | pattern_la1 = _malatya2223h | pattern_ra1 = _gfk2223h }} '''Gaziantep Futbol Kulübü''' is a Turkish professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Gaziantep]]. Founded in 1988, the club plays in the [[Süper Lig]], the highest tier of Turkish football. The club was founded as Sankospor in 1988 and competed at the amateur level until 1993. They competed between the [[TFF Third League]] and [[TFF First League]] until 2019, when they were promoted to the [[Süper Lig]]. During the 2020–21 season, the club reached the top of the standings in week 17, which they held for one week until being overtaken by [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]]. In February 2023, Gaziantep F.K. withdrew from the [[2022–23 Süper Lig]] season following the devastating [[2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes]], which severely impacted the city of [[Gaziantep]] and the club's facilities.{{cite web |date=12 February 2023 |title=Gaziantep FK withdraw from Turkish Super Lig this season following quakes |url=https://www.trtworld.com/turkey/gaziantep-fk-withdraw-from-turkish-super-lig-this-season-following-quakes-65335 |access-date=2026-02-09 |publisher=TRT World}} The [[Turkish Football Federation]] (TFF) accepted the withdrawal request and approved the club's rights to remain in the Süper Lig for the following season, exempting them from relegation despite missing the remainder of the campaign.{{cite web |date=9 February 2023 |title=Hatayspor withdraw from Turkish league after earthquake - clubs union president |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/hatayspor-withdraw-turkish-league-after-earthquake-clubs-union-president-2023-02-09/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |publisher=Reuters}} The club returned to competition for the [[2023–24 Süper Lig]] season, playing their home matches at the [[Gaziantep Stadium|Kalyon Stadium]]. They finished the 2023–24 campaign in 11th place, securing their position in the top flight.{{cite web |date=26 May 2024 |title=Süper Lig wrap: Gaziantep FK secure safety, Istanbulspor relegated |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/super-lig-wrap-gaziantep-fk-secure-safety-istanbulspor-relegated |access-date=2026-02-09 |publisher=Daily Sabah}} In the subsequent 2024–25 season, the team continued to compete in the Süper Lig under the management of [[Selçuk İnan]], who had been appointed head coach in March 2024.{{cite web |date=8 March 2024 |title=Gaziantep FK appoints Selçuk İnan as new manager |url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/gaziantep-fk-appoints-selcuk-inan-as-new-manager-191345 |access-date=2026-02-09 |publisher=Hürriyet Daily News}}"}}
